Objective: Audit every UPDATE statement in the SQL review to ensure it has a bounded WHERE clause that restricts the rows affected.

Target statement types: UPDATE statements only. This rule applies to DML UPDATE changes; it does not apply to other statement types.

Pass criteria: An UPDATE statement passes only when it contains a WHERE clause and that WHERE clause includes at least one row-limiting condition that evaluates to true only for the intended subset of rows. The condition must be explicit and must not be an always-true predicate.

Violation triggers: Flag the UPDATE statement as a violation when any of the following is true: (1) the UPDATE statement has no WHERE clause; (2) the WHERE clause is present but contains only an always-true condition, such as a predicate that is guaranteed to match every row; (3) the WHERE clause does not restrict the affected rows in a meaningful way and therefore permits an unbounded update.
